artworks.title: Title Page for "Views of the Ports of the Sea"
artworks.medium: etching on laid paper
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 9.2 x 13.9 cm (3 5/8 x 5 1/2 in.)
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: The image shows a waterfront scene with ships on the left and workers carrying barrels and sacks from the water to a dock. The background features more workers, boats, and buildings in the distance. The sky is monochrome with fine horizontal strokes, and birds are visible. The image is created using an etching technique, with a detailed and stark visual presentation.

artworks.title: Red-winged Starling, Female Red-winged Starling, Black-poll Warbler, and Lesser Red-poll
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving with etching on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: The image shows four birds. The largest bird is black with red and yellow accents, flying at the top. Below, a starling with a speckled brown and black pattern is perched on a tree stump. Next to it is a smaller bird with white, black, and yellow colors. Further down, there is a bird with a red crown, pink chest, and brown and white back. The color palette includes black, red, brown, white, yellow, and pink. The birds are positioned with the flying black bird at the top, the starling on the left of the stump, the smaller bird on the right of the stump, and the bird with the red crown near a small patch of grass at the bottom.

artworks.title: Pinnated Grous, Blue-green Warbler, and Nashville Warbler
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving with etching on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: This is a painting of three different bird species. The central bird is a pinnated grouse with intricate feather patterns and a yellow-orange spot on its neck. Above this bird, two smaller birds can be seen; one is a blue-grey bird, the blue-grey warbler, with distinct wing patterns, and the other is a small yellow-green bird, the Nashville warbler. In the background, there are subtle details of a pair of birds in a marshy area with water. The style resembles that of John James Audubon, known for detailed depictions of birds in their natural habitats.

artworks.title: Carolina Cuckoo, Black-billed Cuckoo, Blue Yellow-backed Warbler, and Yellow Red-poll Warbler
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving with etching on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: The image shows four birds in various positions on tree branches and the ground. A gray and brown bird sits centrally on a branch, with a smaller bird below it. Another bird with vivid blues and yellows perches on the same branch below the central bird, while a yellow and brown bird is perched higher on another branch. The color palette includes earthy tones and vibrant blues, yellows, and reds. The birds are distributed in different areas of the image, with the gray and brown bird dominating the center, the blue-yellow bird below it, and the other two birds positioned higher and lower on separate branches.

artworks.title: Passenger Pigeon, Blue-mountain Warbler, and Hemlock Warbler
artworks.artist: John G. Warnicke after Alexander Wilson
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving with etching on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: This is a painting of three birds - a pigeon and two smaller birds. The illustration shows a large pigeon perched on a tree stump with detailed plumage of blue, brown, and gray, and a reddish eye. In the foreground, two smaller birds are perched on a branch with bright yellow feathers and black and white accents on their wings and backs. The leaves on the branch are green. The composition and detail reflect a realistic and scientific approach to ornithological illustration.

artworks.title: The Red Bellied Woodpecker (Picus Carolinus)
artworks.artist: Johann Michael Seligmann after Mark Catesby
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: Two large woodpeckers are perched on a tree trunk surrounded by a large, green, heart-shaped leaf. The color palette includes shades of red, brown, green, and black, with the woodpeckers displaying distinctive red heads. The woodpecker on the left is positioned vertically with its head facing to the right, sitting against the tree trunk. The second woodpecker is tilted at an angle on the trunk, facing towards the first, just to the right side. Two small acorns are visible attached to the leaf's branch near the base of the birds.

artworks.title: The Tropic Bird (Phaeton aethereus)
artworks.artist: Johann Michael Seligmann after Mark Catesby
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds. One bird is in flight with wings extended upwards, while the other bird is standing on the ground. The large bird has a long tail, white plumage, a red beak, and red legs. The smaller bird has brown feathers. The composition is detailed and illustrative with a plain background. The image features text in various languages that describe the birds. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon, known for his precise bird illustrations.

artworks.title: The Nuthatch (Sitta Europaea)
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a tree stump surrounded by leafy branches. The tree stump has dark, textured bark and a smooth, flat top, while the branches have elongated green leaves. One bird is on the left side of the stump, displaying black, white, and hints of orange plumage, while the other bird is on the right. Acorns can be seen on the branches. The painting captures the interaction between the birds and their habitat, and is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: The Purple Martin (Hirundo purpurea)
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: A dark blue bird with a long tail sits on a wooden post adorned with green vines and clusters of small red berries. The post and roof have natural wood and straw tones, while the leaves are green and the berries are red.

artworks.title: The Blue Heron (Ardea coerulea)
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on laid paper

artworks.title: The Round Crested Duck (Mergus cucullatus)
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a bird with striking plumage and an open bill. The illustration features a bird with a pronounced crest on its head and an open bill that reveals the texture of the beak. The bird's feathers are intricately detailed, showcasing a mix of dark and light shades. The drawing captures the curve of the bird's neck and the lines of its body, resting on a surface with a neutral background. The composition focuses on the unique features of the bird, with a label 'Mergus' noted beneath the image.

artworks.title: The Buffel's Head Duck (Anas bucephala)
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a duck. The image features a duck standing on a simple ground. The duck is depicted in profile, with a colorful head combining hues of blue and green, accented with white. The feathers on the duck's body are textured with detailed lines in shades of grey and black. The duck's legs and webbed feet are visible, rendered in an earthy tone. The background of the image is bare.

artworks.title: The Rock Fish (Perca venenosa)
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a fish. The artwork shows a fish with a grey body, small red spots, a yellow mark near its gills, detailed fins with dark lines, textured scales, and a vivid reddish-orange eye. Written text below the image identifies the fish as "Perca venenosa (poisonous)" or "The Rock Fish," from the location "Bahamas." It appears to be a historical or botanical illustration for educational or scientific purposes.

artworks.title: The Yellow-breasted Chat
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: A bird with gray wings and a bright yellow belly is perched upon a plant with wide, dark green leaves and vibrant purple flowers. The color palette of the image includes shades of gray, yellow, dark green, and purple against a light, neutral background. The bird is situated above the leaves, with its wings slightly open, while the plant extends downward, showing its roots at the bottom. Detailed textures of the bird's feathers and the plant's leaves and roots are prominent in the composition.

artworks.title: The Soree (Rallus Virginianus)
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: This is a painting of a bird and a flowering plant. The image features a bird standing on a small piece of rocky ground with long legs and a slightly curved beak. Adjacent to the bird is a tall, slender plant with large green leaves and blue flowers. The background is a simple light color, emphasizing the natural elements in the foreground.

artworks.title: The Oyster-catcher (Hoematopus ostralegus)
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a bird standing on a rock with a branch nearby. The bird has a long, slender, red beak and red eyes. It has a brown body with a white patch on its wings and light-colored legs. The rock is textured, and there is a green branch with elongated leaves and two rounded fruits or buds. A simple background is visible with a horizontal line at the bottom. The style suggests a focus on ornithological or botanical illustration.

artworks.title: The Green Lizard of Jamaica (Lacerta bullaris)
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: The image shows a green lizard with a red throat perched on a plant with pink and yellow flowers. The plant has green leaves, pink and yellow flowers, and brown seed pods. The lizard is positioned on a branch with leaves and flowers around it, along with hanging seed pods.

artworks.title: The Lyon Lizard (Lacerta 6-lineata)
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: The image includes a green-stemmed plant with elongated leaves and two prominent flowers, one yellow and the other white. A lizard is on the plant's stem. The color palette consists of green, yellow, gray, and white against a light background. The plant stretches from the bottom to the top of the image, with the lizard positioned in the middle, wrapping its tail around the stem above visible roots at the base.

artworks.title: The Lyon Lizard (Lacerta 6-lineata)
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: The image depicts a plant with elongated green leaves and a flower with long yellow petals and white internal petals. There is a lizard clinging to the plant's stem. The plant's leaves, lizard, and flower are rendered in shades of green, brown, yellow, and white. The plant extends vertically, with the lizard positioned lower on the stem and the flower at the top.

artworks.title: The Land Frog (Rana)
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: The image features a large pitcher plant on the left and another similar plant structure with a rounded, green and red-veined hood on the right, both leaning towards the center. Below them is a yellow and green flower with yellow petals and brown details. At the bottom, there is a small brown frog with a black outline around its red eye in the center. The color palette includes shades of green, brown, yellow, and hints of red.

artworks.title: The Bahama Coney (Mus Monax)
artworks.medium: etching and engraving with hand coloring on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: This is an image of a small rodent surrounded by foliage and berries. The painting features a detailed depiction of a brown-furred rodent with a realistic texture and shading to show its fur and musculature. The rodent is shown on four legs with a slightly curved posture. Its tail extends out behind it, and its ears are perked attentively. Around the animal are branches of foliage with green leaves. Some branches have red berries, while others have blue flowers and buds. The background is minimalistic.

artworks.title: Golden Pheasant (Chrysolophus pictus)
artworks.medium: watercolor over graphite on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green

artworks.title: Green Heron, Night Heron, Young Heron, and Great White Heron
artworks.artist: John G. Warnicke after Alexander Wilson
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving with etching on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: This painting depicts four different species of herons together. The birds are detailed in appearance, showcasing their distinct features and plumage colors. One heron has white plumage and an orange beak, standing on the left. Another heron with turquoise body and chestnut chest is perched on a branch to the right. A dark-capped heron with gray and black wing pattern is shown below, facing the viewer. There is a heron with brown speckles and a red eye under the tall heron. The background features grass, water, and distant landforms, emphasizing the birds. The style is similar to John James Audubon's accurate bird depictions.

artworks.title: Louisiana Heron, Pied Oyster-catcher, Hooping Crane, and Long-billed Curlew
artworks.artist: John G. Warnicke after Alexander Wilson
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving with etching on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Dr. and Mrs. George Benjamin Green
artworks.description: This is a painting of a collection of birds standing near a body of water. The painting depicts four different bird species positioned on the ground near the water's edge. The largest bird, a crane, stands prominently with elongated legs and neck, its feathers detailed in white and grayish shades. Accompanying the crane is a heron with a slender body and pointed beak, showcased by its distinctive blue and white plumage. A black and white oystercatcher is also present, distinguishable by its bright red legs and beak. The fourth bird, a long-billed curlew, is portrayed with brown and tan patterning on its feathers and a notably long, curved bill. The background displays a serene lake with gentle ripples, set against a landscape of distant hills and soft, cloud-filled skies. This is in style of John James Audubon.
